title: How 3-D Printing Can Create Tissue from Stem Cells
main_content: An Israeli company Nano Dimension, uses a specialized 3-D printer to create an environment in which stem cells could grow into tissue. Stem cells can develop into many different kinds of cells in the body. One kind, called induced pluripotent stem cells (IPS), are used to replace tissues. Nano Dimension is partnering with another Israeli company, Accellta, a developer of technologies to produce IPS cells. The companies have yet to produce fully functional human tissue. Amit Dror is the head of Nano Dimension. Special ink containing living stem cells, Dror said. Production of complex tissues, such as full organs, is still years away from happening. So 3-D printing would likely be more successful in producing simpler tissues like skin or muscle.
